questions.question: A hundredths grid is 1 whole square cut into 100 equal small squares. Ravi takes just one of those small squares and cuts it into 10 equal thin strips. What part of the whole grid is ONE thin strip?
questions.explain: Each small square is 1 hundredth, and cutting it into 10 equal strips makes each strip 1 thousandth, so 1 whole = 1000 thousandths. The common trap is answering 0.01 by forgetting that the small square was split again.

questions.question: A hundredths grid is 1 whole cut into 100 equal small squares. Mia shades 4 complete small squares. Then she cuts one more small square into 10 equal strips and shades 7 of those strips. What decimal shows the total shaded amount?
questions.explain: 4 small squares are 4 hundredths and 7 strips are 7 thousandths, so the amount is 0 tenths, 4 hundredths, 7 thousandths = 0.047. The common trap is writing 0.47, which puts the 4 in the tenths place instead of the hundredths place.

questions.question: A hundredths grid is 1 whole cut into 100 equal small squares, and every small square can be cut into 10 equal strips. Leo shades 2 full columns, and each column holds 10 small squares. How many thousandths has Leo shaded?
questions.explain: 2 full columns are 2 tenths = 20 hundredths, and each hundredth is 10 thousandths, so that is 200 thousandths. The common trap is stopping at 20 thousandths by counting the small squares and forgetting the second split into 10.

questions.question: A hundredths grid is 1 whole cut into 100 equal small squares (10 columns of 10), and any small square can be cut into 10 equal strips. Which shading shows exactly 0.106 of the whole?
options: 1 small square shaded, plus 6 strips of another small square
6 full columns shaded, plus 1 strip of another small square
1 full column shaded, plus 6 more whole small squares
1 full column of 10 small squares shaded, plus 6 strips of another small square
questions.explain: 0.106 means 1 tenth (a full column of 10 small squares), 0 hundredths, and 6 thousandths (6 strips of one small square). The common trap is shading only 1 small square, which gives 0.016 because a single small square is a hundredth, not a tenth.

questions.question: A number line runs from 0.24 to 0.25, and the space between them is divided into 10 equal parts. Nooran marks a point on the 3rd mark after 0.24. What decimal is her point?
questions.explain: The gap from 0.24 to 0.25 is one hundredth, so each of the 10 equal parts is one thousandth, and 3 parts past 0.24 is 0.243. The common trap is 0.27, which counts each little part as a hundredth instead of a thousandth.

questions.question: Kai is filling in a place-value chart and needs another way to write 0.4. Which amount is equal to 0.4?
questions.explain: 1 whole = 1000 thousandths, so 1 tenth = 100 thousandths and 4 tenths = 400 thousandths. The common trap is 4 thousandths, which just copies the digit 4 without changing the place-value unit.

questions.question: In science class at a Surrey school, Amara measures 0.75 L of water into a beaker. How many thousandths of a litre is that?
questions.explain: 0.75 L is 75 hundredths, and each hundredth is 10 thousandths, so 0.75 L = 750 thousandths of a litre. The common trap is 75 thousandths, which keeps the digits but skips the change from hundredths to thousandths.

questions.question: On a hike near Squamish, Ben finds a small rock with a mass of 2 tenths and 6 thousandths of a kilogram. Which decimal shows that mass?
questions.explain: Write each place in order: 2 tenths, 0 hundredths, 6 thousandths, which gives 0.206 kg. The common trap is 0.26 kg, which drops the empty hundredths place and slides the 6 into hundredths.

questions.question: Sam says that 0.125 is greater than 0.7 because 125 is bigger than 7. Which statement is correct?
options: 0.7 is greater, because 0.7 is 700 thousandths and 0.125 is 125 thousandths.
0.125 is greater, because it has more digits.
0.125 is greater, because 125 thousandths is more pieces than 7 tenths.
0.125 is greater, because 0.7 is only 70 thousandths.
questions.explain: Rewrite both numbers in the same unit: 0.7 = 700 thousandths and 0.125 = 125 thousandths, so 0.7 is the greater number. The common trap is comparing 125 with 7 as if they were whole numbers, or turning 0.7 into 70 thousandths instead of 700.

questions.question: Priya is doing an experiment with a 1 L jug. She pours in 0.35 L of water, then adds 0.008 L more with a dropper. How many thousandths of a litre are now in the jug?
questions.explain: First change 0.35 L to the same unit: 0.35 L = 350 thousandths, then add the 8 thousandths to get 358 thousandths (0.358 L). The common trap is adding 35 + 8 = 43 without first converting the hundredths into thousandths.

questions.question: A gas station sign in Kamloops shows $1.749 per litre. Overnight the price drops by 20 thousandths of a dollar. What is the new price per litre?
questions.explain: 20 thousandths of a dollar is $0.020, so $1.749 - $0.020 = $1.729. The common trap is treating 20 thousandths as $0.20 and getting $1.549, or as $0.002 and getting $1.747.

questions.question: A number line goes from 0.2 to 0.3, and that space is divided into 10 equal parts. Then the single part between 0.26 and 0.27 is divided again into 10 equal parts. Which decimal sits on the 5th small mark after 0.26?
questions.explain: The first split makes hundredths, and splitting one hundredth into 10 equal parts makes thousandths, so 5 small marks past 0.26 is 0.265. The common trap is 0.31, which counts the tiny marks as hundredths and adds 0.05 instead of 0.005.
